bib.title: Self-Play Fine-Tuning Converts Weak Language Models to Strong Language Models

question: Can a weak SFT LLM improve itself without any additional human-annotated data or stronger-LLM feedback?
hypothesis: Iterated self-play against its own previous-iteration generations, discriminating them from SFT human responses, converges to the data distribution and improves benchmark scores beyond further SFT.
contributions: Propose SPIN, a self-play fine-tuning method starting from an SFT model, needing only the SFT dataset
Prove the global optimum is reached only when the LLM policy equals the target data distribution
Empirically improve zephyr-7b-sft-full on Open LLM Leaderboard, MT-Bench and Big-Bench, matching or exceeding DPO with 62k extra GPT-4 preference data

method.summary: At each iteration the current model generates a response y' for every prompt in the SFT data; the next model is trained with a DPO-like logistic loss to prefer the human SFT response y over y' relative to the previous iterate. Applied to zephyr-7b-sft-full with 50k Ultrachat200k prompts for 4 iterations (0-3), 2 epochs each.
method.task: self-play fine-tuning of an SFT LLM (iterative preference-style optimisation without preference labels)

datasets.name: Ultrachat200k (random 50k prompts, first turn only)
datasets.size: 50k prompts; synthetic set 50k at iter 0, 100k at iters 1-3 (new 50k plus previous 50k)
datasets.split: random 50k sample of the 200k SFT subset
datasets.source: HuggingFaceH4/ultrachat_200k, from UltraChat (~1.4M dialogues from OpenAI Turbo APIs)
datasets.preprocessing: only first round of multi-turn dialogues used as prompt and ground-truth completion

datasets.name: UltraFeedback Binarized
datasets.source: Cui et al. 2023; chosen/rejected judged by GPT-4
datasets.preprocessing: used only for the DPO baseline and the SPIN+DPO row

datasets.name: HuggingFace Open LLM Leaderboard (Arc, TruthfulQA, Winogrande, GSM8k, HellaSwag, MMLU)
MT-Bench, Big-Bench-Hard (causal judgement, sports, formal fallacies), OpenBookQA

models.name: zephyr-7b-sft-full
models.init_from: Mistral-7B SFT on Ultrachat200k by HuggingFace

training.objective: logistic loss l(t)=log(1+exp(-t)) on lambda*log(p_theta(y|x)/p_theta_t(y|x)) - lambda*log(p_theta(y'|x)/p_theta_t(y'|x)), y from SFT data, y' from previous iterate
training.lr: peak 5e-7 for iterations 0 and 1; 1e-7 for iterations 2 and 3
training.lr_schedule: inferred: decay of peak LR across iterations; within-iteration schedule shape not stated
training.regularisation: beta=0.1 (the KL-like temperature, lambda^-1 in the objective), beta=5.0 at iter 3
training.compute: per iteration generation 1.45h; training 4.32h (iter 0) and 8.64h (iters 1-3); per 64 examples generation 6.69s, training 10s
training.wall_clock: inferred: about 5.77h iter 0 and 10.09h per later iteration from Table 2

other.codebase: Alignment Handbook with DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 and FlashAttention-2
other.SPIN+DPO: DPO 2 epochs on 62k UltraFeedback from SPIN iter 3

inference.samples: one synthetic response y' per prompt per iteration; one reported run

other.generation: Accelerate library, distributed inference, global batch size 64; decoding settings not stated

metrics.name: Open LLM Leaderboard average
metrics.definition: mean of Arc acc_norm (25-shot), TruthfulQA mc2 (0-shot), Winogrande acc (5-shot), GSM8k acc (5-shot), HellaSwag acc_norm (10-shot), MMLU acc (5-shot)

eval.protocol: single run per configuration, no seeds, no confidence intervals stated

evidence.quote: We set the peak learning rate to be 5e-7 for iterations 0 and 1, and decay this peak learning rate to 1e-7 for iteration 2 and 3

results.claim: SPIN lifts zephyr-7b-sft-full's Open LLM Leaderboard average from 58.14 to 63.16 over iterations 0-3 with no new preference data.
results.setup: zephyr-7b-sft-full (Mistral-7B SFT on Ultrachat200k), 50k Ultrachat200k prompts, 4 SPIN iterations (0-3), 2 epochs per iteration, single run reported
results.quote: SPIN effectively improves the base model’s average score from 58.14 to 63.16 on the HuggingFace Open LLM Leaderboard

results.metric: Open LLM average, change vs previous iteration
results.table: Table 4, row SPIN iteration 3, column Average

results.claim: Iteration 0 average is 60.80, iteration 1 is 62.12, iteration 2 is 62.97.
results.table: Table 4, row SPIN iteration 0, column Average (iter 1 62.12, iter 2 62.97)

results.claim: Another SFT epoch on Ultrachat200k degrades zephyr-7b-sft-full to 57.23 average, while SPIN improves.
results.setup: zephyr-7b-sft-full fine-tuned 1 more epoch on Ultrachat200k
results.table: Table 5, row SFT epoch 1, column Average

results.claim: zephyr-7b-dpo-full (DPO on ~62k GPT-4-labelled UltraFeedback pairs) scores 61.31; SPIN iteration 0 (60.80) is comparable and iteration 1 (62.12) surpasses it.
results.setup: same SFT checkpoint; DPO row is zephyr-7b-dpo-full (text calls it zephyr-7b-beta); SPIN uses only the existing 50k SFT data
results.note: Section 6.2 calls the DPO model zephyr-7b-beta; Table 3 labels it zephyr-7b-dpo-full.

results.claim: SPIN iteration 0 is comparable to DPO on average, and from iteration 1 surpasses it.
results.quote: SPIN based on the existing SFT data can already achieve comparable average performance to DPO training at iteration 0.

results.claim: Iteration 0 gains are largest on GSM8k (26.76 to 35.10) and TruthfulQA (43.73 to 49.18); iteration 3 reaches GSM8k 38.97 and TruthfulQA 54.90.
results.table: Table 4, row SPIN iteration 3, column GSM8k

results.claim: Winogrande and MMLU do not improve: Winogrande 74.19 to 73.72 and MMLU 60.92 to 59.99 at iteration 3.
results.table: Table 4, row SPIN iteration 3, column MMLU

results.claim: MT-Bench rises from 5.94 to 6.78 by iteration 2; iteration 3 not reported for MT-Bench.
results.setup: zephyr-7b-sft-full vs SPIN iteration 2; MT-Bench judged by Zheng et al. protocol (judge not named in this paper)
results.table: Table 6, row SPIN iteration 2, column MT-Bench

results.claim: Further DPO for 2 epochs on 62k UltraFeedback pairs after SPIN iteration 3 gives 64.05 average (+0.89).
results.setup: SPIN iter 3 then DPO 2 epochs on UltraFeedback Binarized
results.table: Table 3, row SPIN iteration 3 + DPO, column Average

results.claim: Training SPIN for more epochs within iteration 0 plateaus and cannot match iteration 1.
results.setup: 50k synthetic data, iteration 0, epochs up to ~5 (read from Fig 4)
results.quote: extending the training in iteration 0 fails to reach the performance comparable to iteration 1.

results.claim: In the training-size ablation, SFT on epochs 2 and 3 yields under 1% gain while SPIN improves with size (14k, 26k, 50k).
results.setup: SPIN iteration 0, 1 epoch, 14k/26k/50k prompts vs Mistral-7B SFT on Ultrachat200k for 3 epochs
results.quote: SFT on further epochs 2 and 3 fails to yield more than 1% improvement.

results.claim: SPIN adds no preference data cost but generation overhead: 1.45h generation per iteration, training 4.32h (iter 0) and 8.64h (iters 1-3) on 8xA100 80G.
results.setup: 8xA100 (80G), 50k generated examples per iteration; doubled dataset from iter 1
results.table: Table 2, row Iter 1 Training, column Time

results.claim: Authors concede a ceiling: the fixed human target distribution limits the fine-tuned model.
results.setup: theory: optimum only when p_theta = p_data
results.quote: which inherently imposes a ceiling on the performance of fine-tuned LLM

results.claim: Theorem 5.2: global optimum of the SPIN loss is reached iff the model distribution equals the data distribution.
results.setup: convex monotonically decreasing loss; assumes p_theta = p_data is realisable
results.quote: we prove that our method converges when the distribution of the LLM is identical to the target data distribution

limits: Fixed human target distribution imposes a ceiling on performance (Sec 7); improvement approaches zero by iteration 3
Synthetic data generation cost; authors suggest reducing the volume needed
One base model (zephyr-7b-sft-full) and one dataset; single runs, no seeds or intervals reported
MT-Bench reported only to iteration 2; Winogrande and MMLU do not improve
Beta changed to 5.0 at iteration 3 and LR lowered at iterations 2-3, so iteration-wise comparison mixes hyperparameter changes
Theory assumes p_theta=p_data is realisable by the model class; decoding settings for generation not stated
DPO comparison uses a public checkpoint, not re-trained by authors

terms.definition: Main player (new LLM) discriminates opponent (previous-iteration LLM) responses from human SFT responses; opponent is the old model.

lineage.note: SPIN's loss resembles DPO but pairs SFT responses against self-generated ones; no preference data

lineage.work: Zephyr: Direct distillation of LM alignment
lineage.note: base model zephyr-7b-sft-full, DPO baseline, Alignment Handbook
concurrent; explicit LLM-as-judge plus iterative DPO
